posts.author: CreditCardEnthusiast
posts.content: I've been looking at the Chase Sapphire Preferred for a while now. The 60k signup bonus sounds great but I'm wondering if the $95 annual fee is worth it compared to no-fee cards. Anyone have experience with this card?

comments.author: FrequentTraveler99
comments.content: Absolutely worth it if you travel at all. The points transfer to airlines at 1:1 which makes them incredibly valuable. I've gotten over $2000 in value from the card in the past year alone.

replies.author: BudgetMinded
replies.content: That's great if you travel, but for someone who mostly does everyday spending, wouldn't a 2% flat cashback card be better? No annual fee and simpler math.

replies.author: FrequentTraveler99
replies.content: Fair point for non-travelers. But even for dining alone (3x points), the CSP can beat 2% cashback when you value points at 1.5-2 cents each through transfer partners.

comments.author: PointsHacker
comments.content: One thing people overlook: the $50 annual hotel credit effectively makes it a $45/year card. Plus the DoorDash credits. The math works out even for moderate spenders.
